extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for evaluating and preparing affidavits/declarations under 37 CFR 1.130 (AIA first-inventor-to-file context), including when such submissions can disqualify disclosures as prior art and the formal/timeliness/attestation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(1)(A)/102(b)(2)(A) exceptions (1.130(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the disclosure addressed in the affidavit/declaration is subject to the exceptions of 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(1)(A) or 102(b)(2)(A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.130(a) is not available if: (1) the disclosure was made more than one year before the effective filing date of the claimed invention (see MPEP § 2152.01 to determine effective filing date); or (2) the disclosure applied in the rejection is a U.S. patent or U.S. patent application publication that claims the same or substantially the same invention and the affidavit contends that an inventor named in that patent/publication derived the claimed invention from the inventor(s) named in the application. See MPEP § 717.01, subsection II for more on when declarations under 37 CFR 1.130(a) are not available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of facts to establish inventorship or derivation (1.130(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the affidavit/declaration shows sufficient facts, in weight and character, to establish that (1) the disclosure was made by the inventor or a joint inventor, or (2) the subject matter disclosed was obtained directly or indirectly from the inventor or a joint inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider factors such as: an 'unequivocal' statement from the inventor/joint inventor that he/she (or a specific combination of joint inventors) invented the subject matter, accompanied by a reasonable explanation of additional authors, may be acceptable (In re DeBaun). A mere statement without reasonable explanation may be insufficient where contrary evidence exists (e.g., a contrary statement from another named author as in Ex parte Kroger). Evaluation is case-by-case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal requirements of affidavits/declarations (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the affidavit or declaration meets the formal requirements set forth for 37 CFR 1.130 submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 717.01(c) for formal requirements. 37 CFR 1.130 does not include the 1.131(b) provision requiring original exhibits or copies to accompany the affidavit in all cases; however, when additional evidence is required, exhibits must accompany the affidavit/declaration. An affidavit/declaration must be accompanied by any exhibits the applicant or patent owner wishes to rely upon. See specific subsections (e.g., 717.01(c), 717.01(d)) for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the affidavit or declaration is presented timely in relation to the rejection or proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeliness requirements are set out in MPEP § 717.01(f). Examiners must determine whether the affidavit/declaration was filed within the time periods that permit reliance on 37 CFR 1.130.

rubrics_metrics.name: No requirement to show enabling disclosure (1.130 submissions)
rubrics_metrics.description: An affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.130 is not required to demonstrate that the inventor-originated disclosure was an 'enabling' disclosure under 35 U.S.C. 112(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2155.04. The question for 1.130 is origin/derivation/public disclosure by the inventor or someone who obtained it from the inventor, not whether that disclosure met enablement under section 112(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(1)(B)/102(b)(2)(B) exceptions (1.130(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the disclosure applied in the rejection is subject to the exceptions of 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(1)(B) or 102(b)(2)(B) under 37 CFR 1.130(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.130(b) is not available if: (1) the disclosure was made more than one year before the effective filing date; or (2) the disclosure is a U.S. patent or U.S. patent application publication that claims the same or substantially the same invention and the affidavit contends derivation from the inventor named in the application/patent. See MPEP § 717.01, subsection II for more on exceptions availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and dating of prior public disclosure (1.130(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The declaration/affidavit must identify the subject matter publicly disclosed and provide the date of that public disclosure by the inventor, a joint inventor, or another who obtained the subject matter from the inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a specific requirement for 37 CFR 1.130(b) submissions to establish that the subject matter was publicly disclosed prior to the intervening disclosure or effective filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to attach printed publication copy (1.130(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the earlier public disclosure was in a printed publication, the affidavit/declaration must be accompanied by a copy of that printed publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required by 37 CFR 1.130(b)(1). The Office requires a copy so it can determine entitlement to disqualify the later disclosure and because the earlier disclosure might itself be prior art to other pending applications. See MPEP § 717.01(b)(1)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Particularity requirement for non-printed prior disclosures (1.130(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the earlier public disclosure was not in a printed publication, the affidavit/declaration must describe the subject matter with sufficient detail and particularity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This description must enable the Office to determine what subject matter was publicly disclosed on the earlier date by the inventor/joint inventor or another who obtained it from them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extent of exception — only previously disclosed portion excluded
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the portion of the intervening disclosure that was previously in an inventor-originated disclosure is excepted as prior art; other portions remain available as prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For example, if the inventor previously disclosed elements A, B, and C, and a later intervening disclosure adds element D, then only element D (the portion not previously disclosed) remains prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1)/(a)(2) as appropriate. Examiners must consider that a 1.130(b) affidavit may disqualify only part of a cited disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manner/mode and wording of disclosure not determinative
rubrics_metrics.description: The manner or mode of an earlier inventor-originated disclosure (e.g., patenting, publication, public use, sale) and differences in wording are not critical for 37 CFR 1.130(b) to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is not necessary for the inventor-originated disclosure to use the same words or mode as the intervening disclosure. For example, an inventor's slide presentation may disqualify a later journal article disclosure of the same subject matter. The mode/words need not be identical for the exception to apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sameness requirement: 'SAME' is not 'OBVIOUS' (1.130(b)(2) principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: The exceptions under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(1)(B) and 102(b)(2)(B) apply only when the subject matter of the intervening disclosure is the same as the subject matter of the earlier inventor-originated disclosure; an intervening disclosure being obvious over the earlier disclosure does not make it the 'same.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any showing that the intervening disclosure is the same must be sufficient in character and weight to establish identity of subject matter; mere obviousness or derivation of concepts is insufficient to establish sameness for the exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Species/genus and scope relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: How genus/species relationships affect whether an intervening disclosure is 'the same' as an earlier inventor-originated disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an intervening disclosure is a more general description (genus) of subject matter previously disclosed as a species by the inventor, the exception may apply (the genus disclosure is not available as prior art). Conversely, if the earlier disclosure is a genus and the intervening disclosure is a species (more specific), the intervening species disclosure may be available as prior art unless the earlier genus disclosure would have caused a PHOSITA to at once envision every species within that genus. Also, a different species disclosed later that was not disclosed earlier remains prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: No requirement that inventor-filed mode match intervening disclosure mode
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no requirement that the mode (patenting, publication, public use, sale) of the inventor-originated disclosure be the same as the mode of the intervening disclosure for the 102(b) exception to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different modes of disclosure (e.g., slides vs. journal article) do not preclude using a 1.130(b) affidavit to disqualify an intervening disclosure; the Office treats any manner of disclosure as potentially within 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may sign and who must file
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone with knowledge of the facts may sign a declaration under 37 CFR 1.130, but the applicant or patent owner (or a party having authority to act in the application) must be the party that files the affidavit/declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an assignee/obligated assignee/person showing sufficient proprietary interest is the applicant under 35 U.S.C. 118, the applicant or their representative must file the affidavit even if the inventor or another knowledgeable person signed it. Generally, an inventor who is not the applicant lacks authority to file papers in the application. See MPEP § 2155.05.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit attestation formality
rubrics_metrics.description: An affidavit is a written statement made under oath before a notary public, magistrate, or officer authorized to administer oaths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This distinguishes affidavits (sworn statements) from unsworn declarations; formal attestation affects how the statement is executed and may be required depending on the nature of the submission. See MPEP § 717.01(c) for additional formal execution requirements and differences between affidavits and declarations.
